events.title: Tigrayan Forces Cross Tekeze River Into Disputed Tselemt
events.detail: Tigray Defense Forces units crossed the Tekeze River and entered the disputed Tselemti woreda along the Tigray-Amhara boundary, an area contested since the 2020-2022 war. The move triggered direct clashes with the ENDF and Amhara-aligned militias on January 26, 28, and 29, marking the first significant breach of the Pretoria ceasefire in months.

events.title: Clashes Erupt Between ENDF and Tigrayan Forces at Mai Degusha
events.detail: Fighting erupted in Mai Degusha, a contested area within Tselemti district in western Tigray, between Tigrayan fighters and federal forces backed by Amhara militias. Ethiopian Airlines cancelled flights to Tigray cities as a precaution. Getachew Reda, the deposed interim Tigray president, accused 'power-hungry individuals within the TPLF' of trying to drag Tigray into renewed conflict.

events.title: Tigrayan Forces Take Alamata and Korem as Federal Command Withdraws
events.detail: Separate from the Tselemt fighting, Tigrayan forces captured the towns of Alamata and Korem in southern Tigray after the federal command post in the area withdrew. The advance raised fears of a broader collapse of the territorial arrangements set out under the 2022 Pretoria agreement.
events.confidenceReason: Circumstances of the federal withdrawal from Alamata/Korem are disputed between Addis Ababa and Mekelle.

events.title: Drone Strikes Hit Vehicles Near Enticho and Gendebta
events.detail: Drone strikes hit two Isuzu trucks near Enticho and Gendebta in northern Tigray, killing one person and injuring another. Tigrayan officials attributed the strikes to the Ethiopian Armed Forces, though the claim was not independently verified. The incident came amid fears of renewed conflict following the Tselemt and Alamata clashes.
events.confidenceReason: Tigrayan sources blame the ENDF; Addis Ababa has not confirmed responsibility.

events.title: Tigrayan Forces Withdraw From Tselemti, Werede Cites 'Readiness for Dialogue'
events.detail: Tigrayan forces withdrew from Tselemti district. Interim administration security commander Tadesse Werede characterized the withdrawal as demonstrating 'readiness for dialogue and a peaceful resolution,' de-escalating the first round of January clashes. Ethiopian Airlines resumed air services to northern Tigray on February 3.

events.title: Drone Strike Kills Pregnant Woman and Child in North Shewa
events.detail: An ENDF drone strike hit a house in North Shewa zone, Amhara region, killing a pregnant woman, her six-year-old daughter, and a young man. The strike was part of an intensifying pattern of aerial attacks on Fano-controlled areas of Amhara documented by Human Rights Watch's World Report 2026.
events.confidenceReason: ENDF has not confirmed responsibility for individual strikes; HRW attributes the pattern to government forces based on witness testimony.

events.title: East Gojjam Drone Strike Kills 16, Including Children
events.detail: A drone strike in East Gojjam zone killed 16 people, including children, and injured 10 others. The strike is part of a documented pattern of 25 recorded drone and air strikes across seven woredas in six Amhara zonal administrations in the March reporting period alone, which together accounted for 27 civilian deaths and 36 injuries according to monitoring groups.
events.confidenceReason: Government has not acknowledged this specific strike; casualty figures come from local and rights-group monitoring.

events.title: Analysts Warn of Renewed Eritrea-Ethiopia War Risk
events.detail: Horn of Africa analysts and outlets including Martin Plaut renewed warnings that Ethiopia and Eritrea were on a path toward war, citing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's repeated public statements that Ethiopia's access to a Red Sea port — particularly Assab — was 'a matter of time,' and Eritrean mobilization along the border.

events.title: Egypt-Eritrea Maritime Pact Puts Assab and Massawa Back on Red Sea Map
events.detail: A maritime transport agreement between Egypt and Eritrea revived commercial and strategic use of the ports of Massawa and Assab, following an earlier reported December 2025 deal for Egypt to upgrade Assab port infrastructure and expand berths reportedly capable of hosting warships — a development Ethiopian officials viewed warily given Addis Ababa's own ambitions for Assab access.

events.title: Fano Factions Unify Under Amhara Fano National Movement
events.detail: Competing Fano militia factions announced their complete unification, establishing the Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM) under chairman Zemene Kassie, formerly the Gojjam command leader, with veteran Fano leader Eskinder Nega taking the role of Policy and Strategy director and Brig. Gen. Tefera Mamo as military commander. The unified command structure signaled a more coordinated insurgency heading into election season.

events.title: OLA Claims Major Military Gain Within 100km of Addis Ababa
events.detail: The Oromo Liberation Army claimed a significant military operation within roughly 100 kilometers of the capital, saying its fighters killed 256 ENDF troops, wounded 179, and captured 122 others. The government did not confirm the figures, and the claims were not independently verified by outside monitors, but the operation underscored the insurgency's reach toward central Ethiopia ahead of the general election.
events.confidenceReason: Casualty figures are OLA's own claims; the Ethiopian government has not corroborated or denied them, and no independent body has verified the operation.

events.title: ENDF Launches 20,000-Troop Counteroffensive in South Gondar
events.detail: After Fano militias sustained offensives across northern Amhara since March, contesting towns on the B22 and B31 roads leading to the regional capital Bahir Dar, the ENDF reinforced its presence and launched a counteroffensive reported at roughly 20,000 troops to reassert control over South Gondar zone ahead of the June election.

events.title: TPLF Central Committee Holds Emergency Session in Axum
events.detail: The TPLF Central Committee convened an emergency session in Axum, backed by senior military commanders from the party's 'Corps and Above' structures, amid stalled implementation of the Pretoria agreement and Tigray's exclusion from the June general election. The session set the stage for the party's move to reject the federally-extended interim administration.

events.title: TPLF Formally Rejects Extension of Tigray Interim Administration
events.detail: The TPLF issued a formal statement rejecting the federal government's extension of the Tigray Interim Administration (TIA) and calling for the reconstitution of a new regional assembly. Multiple local districts including Wukro, Enticho, and Shiraro publicly endorsed the party's position, deepening the rift with the federally-recognized TIA led by Lt. Gen. Tadesse Worede.

events.title: Explosion Near Regional President's Office in Mekelle Amid Federal Overflights
events.detail: An unexplained explosion occurred near the Regional President's Office in Mekelle as federal military aircraft conducted overhead maneuvers, heightening tensions on the eve of the TPLF's reconstitution of the Tigray regional council.

sources.name: Wikipedia — Reinstatement of the Tigray Regional Council

events.title: TPLF Reconstitutes Tigray Regional Council, Debretsion Sworn In as President
events.detail: The Tigray State Council reconvened for the first time in three and a half years, electing Kiros Hagos as Speaker and TPLF chairman Debretsion Gebremichael as regional president — directly challenging Lt. Gen. Tadesse Worede's federally-backed interim mandate. Debretsion declared: 'The people of Tigray did not struggle for a temporary appointment from Addis Ababa.' The move effectively created a parallel governance structure and was seen by Addis Ababa and international observers as voiding key provisions of the Pretoria agreement.

sources.name: Wikipedia — Reinstatement of the Tigray Regional Council

events.title: TPLF Restructures Tigray Regional Bureaus Under New Council
events.detail: The reconstituted Tigray council restructured regional executive bureaus, appointing Amanuel Assefa as Deputy President and head of the Justice Bureau, consolidating TPLF control over regional administration in parallel to the federally-recognized Tigray Interim Administration.

sources.name: Wikipedia — Reinstatement of the Tigray Regional Council

events.title: Rights Group Documents Forced Recruitment Across Tigray Zones
events.detail: Human Rights First Ethiopia documented forced recruitment allegations across three Tigray zones, collecting 27 witness testimonies, as the TPLF-controlled council prepared a wartime mobilization law with proposed criminal penalties for evasion and for speech discouraging recruitment.

sources.name: Wikipedia — Reinstatement of the Tigray Regional Council

events.confidenceReason: TPLF authorities have not publicly responded to the forced-recruitment allegations.

events.title: At Least 37 Orthodox Christians Killed in East Arsi Zone Attacks
events.detail: Coordinated attacks beginning May 30 in Teleta Gebriel, a remote locality in Aseko district roughly 18km from Aseko town in Oromia's East Arsi Zone, killed at least 37 Orthodox Christians and burned churches over the following days, continuing through the June 1 national election. Local reports described OLA militants selectively targeting members of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church; the group has denied deliberately targeting civilians.
events.confidenceReason: OLA denies deliberately targeting civilians; death toll and attribution vary by source.

events.title: General Election Held Amid Fano Attacks; Tigray Boycotts Entirely
events.detail: Ethiopia held its seventh general election on June 1. Fano militia attacks forced cancellation of voting in 8 constituencies across Amhara, and security incidents kept at least 143 polling stations closed across Amhara and Oromia, collectively preventing an estimated 5-6 million registered voters from participating. Voting did not take place at all in Tigray for the second consecutive cycle. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed condemned the violence and extended condolences to victims of the East Arsi attacks.

events.title: Fighting Recorded in 64 Woredas Across Amhara During Election Week
events.detail: In the week of June 1-7, fighting between Fano and government forces was recorded in more than 64 woreda/city administrations across 12 zonal administrations of Amhara region, according to monitoring by pro-Fano outlets, illustrating the geographic breadth of the insurgency during the election period.
events.confidenceReason: Figures sourced from a pro-Fano monitoring outlet; not independently corroborated.

events.title: NEBE Declares Prosperity Party Winner With 90% of Contested Seats
events.detail: The National Election Board of Ethiopia declared the ruling Prosperity Party winner of the general election, securing 438 of 486 contested seats (about 90%) in the House of Peoples' Representatives. Results in 15 constituencies required a re-run or remained unconfirmed, while voting had been postponed in 46 others across Tigray and Amhara due to security concerns — leaving Abiy Ahmed's renewed mandate unevenly distributed across the country.

events.title: Tigray Council Drafts Wartime Mobilization Law
events.detail: The Legal Standing Committee of the TPLF-controlled Tigray council prepared a draft wartime mobilization proclamation, including proposed criminal penalties for draft evasion and for speech discouraging recruitment, formalizing the region's shift toward a war footing ahead of the August clashes.

sources.name: Wikipedia — Reinstatement of the Tigray Regional Council

events.title: Isaias Afwerki Accuses Ethiopia of Preparing for War Over Red Sea Access
events.detail: In a televised interview, Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki accused Ethiopia of making 'unbalanced statements' and preparing to wage war on Eritrea, describing Addis Ababa's drive to secure Red Sea port access as 'the plan of a crazy person.' Afwerki warned that Eritrea, despite its far smaller population of 3.5 million against Ethiopia's roughly 130 million, would not be easily overpowered.

events.title: ENDF-TPLF Battle at Shererina Marks Most Serious Breach of Pretoria Deal
events.detail: Armed clashes broke out around Shererina, roughly 25 miles south of Humera near the Sudanese border, beginning around 6:00am and lasting until roughly 5:00pm. The fighting involved heavy artillery, drones, and mechanized units, and reportedly involved a TPLF unit known as 'Army 70,' said to be based across the border in Sudan. The TPLF accused the ENDF of initiating the clashes, a claim Addis Ababa disputes. Analysts described it as the most serious incident since the November 2022 Pretoria agreement, occurring roughly two months after the TPLF's reinstatement of the pre-war regional government voided key provisions of the deal.

events.title: Fighting Ends at Shererina, but Calm Remains Fragile
events.detail: Active fighting around Shererina subsided after roughly 11 hours of clashes, though both ENDF and TPLF forces remained mobilized in the area and observers warned the calm was fragile given the collapse of the political arrangements underpinning the Pretoria ceasefire.

events.title: Hundreds of Tigrayans, Including Wounded Fighters, Flee Into Sudan
events.detail: Hundreds of Tigrayans, including wounded fighters, fled into Sudan following the Shererina clashes. Drone or artillery fire caused explosions in several refugee camps near the border, though casualty figures were not immediately available. UNHCR expressed concern about the risk to civilians and refugees already displaced by Sudan's own civil war.

events.title: Amnesty International Warns of Renewed Human Rights Risk in Tigray
events.detail: Amnesty International reported that violent clashes between Tigrayan forces and the ENDF on August 1 put Tigray residents at renewed risk of human rights violations, calling on both sides to protect civilians as the region's political and military crisis deepened.

events.title: Analysts Map 'Tsimdo' — the Alleged Anti-Government Coalition
events.detail: Coverage of northern Ethiopia's shifting alliances examined 'Tsimdo,' a purported coalition linking Eritrean actors, TPLF hardliners, and other opponents of the federal government, first publicly alleged in an October 2025 letter from Ethiopian official Gedion Timothewos to the UN Secretary-General. Neither the Eritrean government nor the TPLF has confirmed any formal alliance, and analysts describe it as cooperation between groups with little in common beyond opposition to Addis Ababa, rather than a unified command.
events.confidenceReason: Existence and structure of the alleged 'Tsimdo' coalition is disputed by the accused parties themselves.

events.title: Drone Strike Hits Merewa Secondary School in Raya Alamata
events.detail: A drone strike hit Merewa Secondary School in Raya Alamata district, roughly 50km west of Alamata town, reportedly using Turkish-made drones dropping 12 bombs. Tigrayan military sources said three fighters stationed at the school died instantly and seven more were hospitalized. District governor Daniel Tamrat instead reported one civilian killed and four wounded, and said a nearby river where residents fetched water was also struck. The school was on holiday break at the time. Repeated follow-on drone strikes were reported in Raya Alamata the same morning.
events.confidenceReason: Tigrayan military sources and the local district governor gave conflicting casualty breakdowns (fighters vs. civilians) for the same strike.

events.title: Eritrean Opposition Figure Describes Tsimdo as Coalition of Divergent Interests
events.detail: A member of an Eritrean opposition central committee publicly described the alleged 'Tsimdo' coalition as uniting anti-Ethiopian-government actors with sharply divergent interests rather than a coherent political-military alliance, following a May 2026 gathering held under the Tsimdo banner in Port Sudan attended by Sudanese army officers, Eritrean officials, and Ethiopian opposition figures.
